physiological-resilience.short: Andrew Jones's name for durability: how well VO₂max, thresholds and efficiency hold up as fatiguing exercise goes on. He proposes it as a fourth factor in endurance performance.

kj-per-kg.short: The mechanical work already done in a ride, in kilojoules, divided by body mass. Used as a fatigue clock: 30 kJ·kg⁻¹ is 2,100 kJ for a 70 kg rider.

mean-maximal-power.short: The highest average power a rider produced over a given duration (10 s, 5 min, 20 min…) in a ride, a period or a season.

record-power-profile.short: A rider's best mean maximal power for each duration, from seconds to hours, joined into one curve.

decoupling.short: When internal load (heart rate, breathing) and external load (power or pace) drift apart during a long effort: heart rate creeps up at the same power, or pace falls at the same heart rate.

emg.short: Recording the electrical signals of active muscle, here with sensors stuck on the skin. How big and how fast the signals are hints at how many and which motor units are working.

polarised-training.short: A way of spreading training intensity: most time easy (below the first threshold), a smaller share hard (above the second), and little in between.
